August, 2025

 In The Court Of Ms. Deepti Devesh

1. The present appeal has been preferred by the prosecution against the impugned judgment dated 22.12.2022 of Ld. MM-06, Patiala House Courts, passed in FIR No.
68/2007, PS Parliament Street, U/s 420/468/471 IPC.
By way of the said impugned judgment respondent Ramadhar Prasad has been acquitted of all the alleged offences.

For the sake of convenience, both parties shall be referred as their original position before the Ld. Trial Court, i.e. as State (appellant) and accused (respondent).
2.
The facts relevant for deciding the present appeal, in brief are as follows.
The accused was appointed as Farash on temporary basis in the office of Press Information Bureau, Shashtri Bhawan, New Delhi, and subsequently, absorbed as a Peon on temporary basis.

He had submitted photocopy of his ST caste certificate No.
68 dated 07.05.1988 and one original ST caste certificate no. 105 dated 21.08.2003,
to his employer for the purposes of employment.
Both the certificates were sent by the employer for verification.

Initially, letter no. 34 dated 09.01.2006 was received qua certificate no. 68 dated 07.05.1988, which stated that the said certificate was The State Govt Of Nct Of Delhi vs Ramadhar Prasad on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195102397/
1 fake.

entities.text: State Govt Of Nct Of Delhi vs Ramadhar Prasad
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Subsequently, letter no. 1236 dated 06.12.2006 was received, which stated that certificate no. 105 dated 21.08.2003 was correct and genuine.
The employer, who is the complainant, decided to get both the caste certificates as well as the above said letters re-verified.
After re-verification, both the caste certificates were found to be fake and letter no. 1236 dated 06.12.2006 was also found to be fake.
Thereafter, the employer gave complaint on which the present FIR was registered.
3. After completion of investigation, chargesheet was filed before court and cognizance of offences punishable u/s 420/468/471 IPC was taken.

Charges for the said offences was framed against the accused on 08.10.2008 and after completion of evidence and arguments, judgment of acquittal was pronounced by the Ld. Trial Court vide the impugned judgment dated 22.12.2022.

4. Now, the State has filed the present appeal challenging the impugned judgment on the following grounds:
a) that the Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate the verification letters disclosing both certificates as fake in the right perspective.
b) that the accused covered up the first caste certificate by producing a second caste certificate and then forging letter no. 1236 saying it to be a genuine caste certificate.
c) that the Ld. Trial court failed to appreciate that all the fake documents were given to obtain employment in a government office by the accused.
d) that the Ld. Trial court has erred in appreciating the evidence led by prosecution and lack of personal knowledge of complainant as to whether the accused was actually appointed as peon on the basis of caste certificate, cannot be read as admission of the claim of accused that he did not use caste certificate to obtain employment.

e) that the Ld. Trial court has assumed that regularisation of accused as an employee barred the department from re-verifying the documents of accused of the basis of which the employment was initially obtained.
5. The State has reiterated the abovesaid averments in its appeal at the time of advancing oral arguments on the present appeal by Ld. Addl. PP for State.
6. Per contra, the accused has challenged the grounds raised on the present appeal.
No written reply to the present appeal has been filed, but oral arguments have been advanced on behalf of accused.
It has been submitted by the accused that the prosecution has failed to establish its case beyond reasonable doubt that the accused had obtained employment on the basis of caste certificate.

He has further argued that the Ld. Trial Court has rightly appreciated that the accused was already The State Govt Of Nct Of Delhi vs Ramadhar Prasad on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195102397/
2 regularised as a peon, when the process of verification was being conducted and therefore, after his regularisation, the process of verification itself was vitiated.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It has been further argued that the prosecution never produced any evidence to establish that the accused had created the alleged forged caste certificates, despite the fact that its own witness PW6 has deposed that one Jairam had provided the said caste certificate to accused.
The accused had further submitted that the impugned judgment does not suffer from any illegality or infirmity and has been correctly passed based on the prevailing law of the land.
7. Arguments have been heard.
Record has been perused.
Trial court record was also summoned and same has been perused.
8. The accused faced trial for offences punishable u/s 420/468/471 IPC.

The essential ingredients required to be proved beyond reasonable doubt for offence punishable u/s 420 IPC by the prosecution against the accused are - a. dishonest inducement of complainant (i) to deliver any property, and b. wrongful loss caused to complainant, or c. wrongful gain caused to accused, on account of such dishonest inducement.
9. The essential ingredients required to be proved beyond reasonable doubt for offence punishable u/s 468 IPC by the prosecution against the accused are - a. The accused forged the document b.
The accused forged the document intending that the forged document would be used for the purpose of cheating.

10. The essential ingredients for establishing offence punishable under Sections 471 IPC are as under:
a. Fraudulent or dishonest use of a false document as genuine by accused.
b. Accused had the knowledge or reason to believe that the document used is a forged one.
11. The prosecution has examined seven witnesses during trial.

The material witnesses were PW1,
PW3, PW4 and PW7.

The gist of their respective testimonies is aptly contained in para numbers 4,6,7 and 10 of the impugned judgment and the said paragraphs may be read as a part of the present judgment, which are not being reproduced herein for the sake of brevity.
12. Firstly, the impugned judgment in relation to offence punishable u/s 468 IPC shall be dealt with.
The Ld. Trial court has reasoned that there was insufficient material to establish that the accused even attempted to forge ST certificate Ex.PW1/B, which is ST certificate no.68 dated 07.05.1988.
However, the impugned judgment is silent as to whether there was sufficient material to link the accused as creator of the other forged certificate i.e. ST certificate no.105 dated 21.08.2003.
Only on this basis, the Ld. Trial court has proceeded to acquit accused for offence punishable u/s 468 IPC.

3 13.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: At this juncture, it is relevant to understand that definition of a forged document under IPC.

As per Section 463 IPC, a forged document is, 'Whoever makes any false document or false electronic record or part of a document or electronic record with intent to cause damage or injury to the public or to any person, or to support any claim or title or to cause any person to part with property, or to enter into any express or implied contract, or with intent to commit fraud or that fraud may be committed, commits forgery.'
14.
The above said definition has been explained by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the judgments of Mohd. Ibrahim v. State of Bihar Crl.

entities.text: Mohd. Ibrahim v. State of Bihar Crl
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Appeal no. 1695 of 2009 decided on 04.09.2009 and in Sheila Sabastian v. R.Jawaharaj in Crl.

entities.text: Sheila Sabastian v. R.Jawaharaj in Crl.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Appeal nos. 359-360 of 2010 decided on 11.05.2018.
In the above said judgments, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has held that the definition of false document has to be read as part of the definition of forgery.

Thus, an accused who is stated to have created a false document, can be said to be guilty of committing forgery under IPC.
15.

In the instant matter, the observation of Ld. Trial Court that there is no material to link the accused as having created the fake ST certificate no.68 Ex.PW1/B is correct on the basis of Trial court record.
Further more, there is no evidence produced by the prosecution during trial that the accused is the creator of caste certificate no. 105 Ex.P1.
Merely because it is the accused who has submitted the said caste certificates before his employer, it can not be presumed that he is the creator of the said documents.

The prosecution's case has to stand on its own legs and no presumption is available in favor of the prosecution, which has to necessarily discharge the burden of proof, which standard is beyond reasonable doubt.

Thus, for lack of any evidence linking the accused as creator of the said caste certificates or letter no.1236, which was also found to be fake subsequently, is sufficient to acquit the accused for offence punishable u/s 468 IPC.

In this regard,
there is no infirmity or illegality in the impugned judgment.
16. Now, coming to the question whether accused can be held guilty of committing offence punishable u/s 420 IPC on the basis of material produced before the Ld. Trial Court.
The Ld. Trial Court has held that the prosecution witness i.e. PW1 herself has admitted in her testimony that the accused already stood regularized when she had joined the department.

It has also been reasoned by the Ld. Trial Court that the prosecution only produced register pertaining to scheduled castes only,
despite the fact that both the caste certificates were in relation to scheduled tribes.

It has been also reasoned by Ld. Trial Court that prosecution failed to establish the mode and manner in which it was verified that the said caste certificates and letter no. 1236 were fake and forged documents, and only reliance has been placed upon the communications received by the department in this regard i.e. letter no. 34 dated 09.01.2006 and letters no. 539 and 540, both dated 11.04.2007.

The Ld. Trial Court has heavily relied upon the oral testimony of PW1 in order to hold that the prosecution failed to establish any wrongful gain to accused or wrongful loss to the department on account of his employment with the department, as the prosecution failed to show that the accused had obtained employment with the department, against a reserved ST category seat, on the basis of the forged caste certificates.

17. Perusal of the trial court record shows that PW3 Umakant Poddar, who was one of the officers appointed for the purpose of verification of the caste certificates of accused has relied upon The State Govt Of Nct Of Delhi vs Ramadhar Prasad on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195102397/
4 documents Ex.PW3/A (colly for 16 pages).

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The set of documents Ex.PW3/A contains the application form of accused (Satyapan form of accused), by way of which the accused had initially given disclosures for his employment with the concerned department.
In Column no.9 of the said document, accused himself has given the declaration that he belongs to Hindu Religion and is a member of the Scheduled Tribe Kharia.

At the end of the said application form, accused has duly signed at the allocated place, with date of application i.e. 07.03.1997, below the declaration that states that he had given all the information in the above said application form, which is true and correct.

Apart from the above document in Ex.PW3/A, PW1 has also produced document Ex.PW1/J (OSR), which was the letter of appointment issued to accused dated 27.02.1997 for his initial appointment as Farash in temporary capacity.
The terms and conditions of the said appointment letter at Serial no. 4, categorically states that "nimnnlikhit pramaan patra prastut karne honge-".
Then Serial no. 4 (kha) states "anusuchit jatiyon / anusuchit janjati samudaye abhyarthi apne is daven ke samarthan mein nirdharit form mein praman patra ".

Thus, the said document Ex.PW1/J (OSR), when read alongwith his initial Satyapan form, where he had mentioned himself to be belonging to scheduled tribe, categorically shows that the defence taken by accused and relied upon by the Ld. Trial court, that the accused never got his appointment as Farash on the basis of accused belonging to scheduled tribe, is incorrect.
He had specifically made the disclosure of belonging to a Scheduled Tribe, for which he knew he will have to produce certificate as per Ex.PW1/J (OSR).
Thus, it belies logic as to why accused would declare himself to be belonging to Scheduled Tribe in his Satyapan form, if his appointment was not under ST category.

If the defense of accused is assumed to be correct, then accused would have not needed to declare himself as an ST in his Satyapan form, to ensure his sustainability in employment with the department.
The Ld. Trial Court has failed to appreciate these material documents that were produced by the prosecution in trial and has only relied upon oral testimonies of witnesses to acquit the accused.
18. During trial, the accused has not disputed the said documents Ex.PW3/A (Colly) and Ex.PW1/J(OSR).
There is no objection of accused recorded to the said documents in the testimony of PW3.
The objection taken by accused to document Ex.PW1/J (OSR), in the testimony of PW1 is that the said document has been produced by a witness who has not executed the said document.
Admittedly, the signatures on document Ex.PW1/J is that of one T.S. Arasu.

The document Ex.PW1/J (OSR) has been produced by the witness as part of the record available in the department,
where PW1 was employed at the time of giving complaint.

Thus, she has nowhere claimed in her testimony that she has personal knowledge regarding Ex.PW1/J (OSR), rather her case is that she is producing all the relevant records in relation to accused as available in the department.

The accused,
has not challenged the authenticity of the said document Ex.PW1/J (OSR), as a fake or false document.
In fact, the original of the document has been produced before the Ld. Trial Court, before being exhibited in evidence.

Thus, the objection relating to execution of document Ex.PW1/J(OSR)
being produced by PW1 is not sustainable and the said document cannot be held to be inadmissible only on this objection of accused.

19. It is pertinent to note here that accused had raised objections to some documents during the testimony of PW1, but no observations or decision in regard to the objections of accused have been decided by the Ld. Trial Court vide the impugned judgment.
Thus, the impugned judgment is incomplete in this regard and liable to be set aside on this ground alone.

Notwithstanding the lack of The State Govt Of Nct Of Delhi vs Ramadhar Prasad on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195102397/
5 decision on objections of the accused by Ld. Trial Court

entities.text: State Govt Of Nct Of Delhi vs Ramadhar Prasad
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , it is pertinent to note that accused had raised objections to documents Ex.PW1/F (OSR), Ex.PW1/G (OSR), and Ex.P2(OSR) in testimony of PW1.
The objection to Ex.P2 (OSR) is same as that of Ex.PW1/J (OSR).
Therefore, for the same reasons as discussed above, objections to Ex.P2 (OSR) is not sustainable.
Ex.PW1/F (OSR) and Ex.PW1/G (OSR), are not required to be decided as neither the Ld. Trial Court nor the present court is basing the reasoning for its decision on the said documents.

Be that as it may, the objections on merits to Ex.PW1/F and Ex.PW1/G (OSR) are not sustainable for the same reasons as discussed qua objection to document Ex.PW1/J (OSR).
20.

Furthermore, even no suggestion has been given to PW3 by accused that the original attested documents, i.e. the Satyapan form of accused dated 07.03.1997, as part of Ex.PW3/A (colly) is false and fabricated document.
Similarly, accused has not given such suggestion to PW1 also regarding Ex.PW1/J (OSR).
Thus, the accused has nowhere challenged, during the entire trial the authenticity of the above said documents.
In this situation, the authenticity of the said documents is undisputed.
Thus, as already discussed above, in light of the above said documents, the defence of accused that he was never appointed on the basis of his ST certificate is not tenable.

He had applied under the ST category and as per the terms and conditions of his initial appointment itself as Farash, he had to provide the necessary documentation in support of his application under the ST category.
21. Furthermore, it is not only the question of initial appointment of accused, that would bring him within the ambit of section 420 IPC.
The accused continued to sustain himself in employment till verification of the caste certificates by the department could be concluded.

As it has been established that both the caste certificates furnished by accused, was not genuine, then continued employment of accused on the strength of the said caste certificates till its verification, amounted to continuing wrongful gain to accused, upon his dishonest inducement on the basis of fake caste certificates given to the department.

Continuous receipt of salary till the time accused was employed with the department till conclusion of verification of caste certificate, amounted to delivery of property for the purpose of section 420 IPC.
22.
The accused has claimed that falsity of his caste certificates has not been established as PW4 has categorically deposed that only SC certificate register was produced.

The accused has also claimed that prosecution did not independently establish the authenticity of letters i.e. letter no. 34 dated 09.01.2006, letter no. 539 and 540 both dated 11.04.2007 to support its claim of falsity of caste certificates.

Perusal of record shows that at the time of evidence, accused has not challenged the authenticity of the above said letters,when they were produced in evidence before court i.e.
Ex.PW1/C (OSR) dated 28.08.2012, Ex.P3 (OSR) and Ex.P4 (OSR).

The original of all the said letters has been produced before court and no material can be found on record to show that the said letters did not originate from the concerned offices as stated therein or were not received in the office of employer of accused or that they had been tampered with, in any manner when produced before Ld. Trial Court, or the contents of the said letters are unreliable for any reason.
23. The Ld. Trial Court has also heavily relied upon the testimony of PW4 in acquitting the accused.

PW4 in his cross examination, PW4 has admitted that he had produced only the SC caste certificate The State Govt Of Nct Of Delhi vs Ramadhar Prasad on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195102397/
6 register, and not the ST caste certificate register.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It has been held by Ld. Trial Court that the accused had produced ST caste certificate and therefore, it stands to reason that the details of his ST caste certificate would not be found in SC caste certificate register.
However, the Ld. Trial Court has failed to appreciate the explanation offered by PW4 in this regard, in its correct context.

PW4 has deposed,
"it is correct that it is mentioned on the register that the register in question pertains to Scheduled Caste.
Vol. Our office does not used to maintain in the year 2002-03 any register for Scheduled Tribes as there were no Scheduled Tribes in that district".
PW4 has categorically stated that no register was being maintained due to no Scheduled Tribes living in that district in 2002-03.

However, his statement cannot be twisted to mean that only in year 2002-03, Scheduled Tribes were not living in that district while they were living in that district prior to 2002-03 or after 2002-03.

The correct meaning of the testimony of PW4 in this regard can be understood from the contents of previously proved documents during trial i.e. letter no. 34 dated 09.01.2006 and letter no. 539 & 540, both dated 11.04.2007.

In letter no. 34 dated 09.01.2006,
Ex.PW1/C (OSR) dated 28.08.2012, it is clearly mentioned that in Saran District, the population of Scheduled Tribes was 'Zero'.

Thus, even at the time of issuance of letter Ex.PW1/C (OSR) dated 28.08.2012, it was categorically mentioned that no Scheduled tribes reside in that district, which was reaffirmed by PW4 in his testimony.
Thus, the caste certificates were indeed fake has duly been established by the above said documents i.e. Ex.PW1/C (OSR) dated 28.08.2012, Ex.P3(OSR) and Ex.P4 (OSR).
24. Now, coming to offence punishable u/s 471 IPC.

Having established that the caste certificates were produced by the accused were indeed fake documents, no doubt remains that accused had used the said fake caste certificates in order to sustain himself in employment with the department.
Accused has never disputed during trial that he had not furnished the caste certificates to the department, when documents were asked by the department.

Thus, it is the accused himself who has used false documents i.e. caste certificate no. 68 dated 07.05.1988 and certificate no. 105 dated 21.08.2003, in order to sustain himself in employment, despite knowing that the said caste certificates were fake documents.
25. In view of the above discussion, the prosecution has successfully proved its case against the accused namely Ramadhar Prasad beyond reasonable doubt.

The prosecution has established that accused had sustained himself in employment with the department on the basis of caste certificate no. 68 dated 07.05.1988 and certificate no. 105 dated 21.08.2003, which were fake documents and thus caused wrongful gain to himself.

Accordingly, he stands convicted for the commission of offences punishable u/s 420/471 IPC.
26.
Copy of this judgment be given free of cost to convict.
